description: Pinned build inputs for the Motion Canvas render path (P2.3-C). Every entry records what is pinned, how it is pinned, where it came from, and what the pin cannot promise. `lces supply-chain-check` audits the record against the Dockerfile, lockfiles and CI workflows; a record without a matching consumer is not a control.

base_image.notes: Multi-arch index digest resolved from the ghcr.io registry API. The tag is kept next to the digest for readability; only the digest is authoritative. Upgrade in a dedicated change that records the new digest and rebuilds the offline image.

node_distribution.notes: SHA-256 copied from the official release directory's SHASUMS256.txt (which is accompanied by SHASUMS256.txt.sig). The checksum is verified inside the image build; the signature is not verified by LCES, so the trust anchor is the official release channel, not a local signature check.

npm_registry.notes: The lockfile resolved to registry.npmmirror.com until P2.3-C. Content was hash-identical (npm ci verified every integrity value against this registry), but the mirror is not the upstream publisher, so the default decision is the official registry.

playwright_browser.source: Playwright CDN selected by the pinned Playwright version
playwright_browser.notes: Playwright downloads its own Chromium build and verifies it against checksums bundled in the package. LCES does not record the browser archive hash separately; CI records the resolved executable path and version per job.

ffmpeg.notes: Installed from the Debian trixie apt repository. The exact build is recorded in every encode report; byte-identical encoding across distro builds is not promised.

node_lock.notes: Only npm ci is admitted; npm install may rewrite versions. The adapter refuses to render when the installed direct dependencies disagree with the lockfile.

python_lock.notes: PyPI packages resolved through uv.lock; CI and the offline image install with --locked, so a stale lockfile fails instead of silently re-resolving.

github_actions.notes: Workflows reference the 40-character commit SHA; the readable tag stays in a trailing comment. A tag is mutable, a commit SHA is not. Upgrade by resolving the new tag and updating both the workflow and this record.
